c: Different studies point to different parts of the system, and some findings depend on medication history. ADHD is better described as several routes to a similar set of difficulties.
The simple version — "ADHD is low dopamine" — is too simple. Some studies find lower dopamine markers, some find higher, and some differences appear to be adaptations to treatment rather than causes.

c: In 53 unmedicated adults, dopamine transporter and D2/D3 receptor binding were lower in reward-pathway regions than in controls, and lower binding correlated with inattention.

Across nine imaging studies, transporter density was on average 14% higher in ADHD, but strongly dependent on prior stimulant exposure: lower in drug-naive people and higher in previously medicated people.
: different combinations of genetic and developmental differences can produce similar day-to-day difficulties.
: the system re-tunes after long-term treatment, changing what a scan shows.
: prefrontal cortex and striatum regulate dopamine differently.

Heterogeneity is not a weakness of the ADHD concept. It is what you expect from a polygenic, developmental condition — and it predicts that people will differ in which medicine, dose and formulation suits them, which is what clinical experience shows.
